thread:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary rollout started for release=fastpath-v2 on cluster=eu-west-1 (canary-id=cp-7265)

maria: heads-up — kicking off a small canary (5%) for fastpath-v2. putting extra healthchecks for kv-cache and long-seq perf. will watch metrics for 10m.

pager-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate detected for service=fastpath-worker (canary pool) — 5xx spike from 0.3% -> 4.8% over 2m. Link: https://grafana.redwood/canary/cp-7265

raj: seeing the alert. looking at pod logs and LB responses. grabbing prometheus and traces now.

maria: oncall? is this hitting user traffic or synthetic probes only?

tess: both. synthetic health probes failing with 502/504, a subset of real requests from eu-west show latency+5xx.

leo: digging into logs — rsa-fastpath-0 container shows recurring stacktrace: 
```
ERROR: runtime error: cache miss during kv-restore -> upstream timed out after 30s
at handler.go:214
```
Repeat 3k lines in 6m.

raj: looks like a regression in the cached prefix load path. load spikes when sequence length > 4096. our canary model uses longer context.

maria: this matches what we saw in perf testing but slipped through. abort criteria in the rollout playbook says abort if 5xx > 2% for 5m. we're currently at 4.8% for 3m. recommend immediate mitigation.

tess: proposals: 1) flip feature flag (fastpath.enabled=false) to stop traffic to canary 2) reweight traffic away from canary to stable 3) scale down canary pool and evict pods. which do we want first?

raj: do flag flip first (lowest blast radius). I can flip and verify within 30s.

maria: agreed. go for flag flip, then traffic reweight if still noisy. ping support to prepare a customer-facing note.

raj: executing flag flip now: 
```
# toggle via config service
curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/flags/fastpath -d '{"enabled":false,"env":"eu-west-1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag fastpath.enabled set to false in eu-west-1 (actor=raj). Rolling config propagation to edge nodes.

pager-bot: :information_source: 30s after flag flip, 5xx rate dropped to 1.1%. Latency normalized on synthetic probes.

maria: nice. that dropped it under abort threshold. still want to unwind the canary to be safe.

tess: initiating traffic reweight now: shifting from 5% -> 0% over 60s.

leo: evicting canary pods to force redeploy and remove stateful caches: 
```
kubectl scale deploy/fastpath-canary --replicas=0 -n prod-eu
```

samir: acknowledged, taking over on-call for the evening — I'm on the handoff. leaving the remaining follow-ups to a postmortem.

maria: thanks samir. support-bot, please create an incident ticket and draft a short customer update that we can send to impacted accounts (brief, non-technical).

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-02 created. Draft message: "We briefly saw increased error rates for Fastpath in eu-west affecting a subset of users. The release was halted and traffic routed away; service is stable. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Waiting on approval from @maria.

maria: approve. add estimated impact: ~0.02% of requests during the 7m window, some long-context LLM generation jobs retried.

raj: quick triage notes: root cause appears to be regression in kv-restore path when sequence lengths exceed 4k causing upstream timeouts and cascading 502s. Repro in staging with long prompt.

tess: mitigation checklist for postmortem: - add unit/regression tests for long-seq kv path - add preflight metric gating for context length distribution to rollout playbook - make the feature flag default-to-off for new model variants - add tighter circuit-breaker on kv upstream timeouts

leo: logs saved to s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2620001234/ and perf traces to jaeger link: https://jaeger.redwood/canary/cp-7265

samir: handing off to night shift. I will monitor alerts for next 2 hours and escalate if anything regresses.

maria: final check — are any enterprise customers impacted enough to require dedicated outreach / credits? support-bot: list attached: customerA (minor), customerB (retrying), customerC (no).

support-bot: Notifying account reps for customerA and customerB. :email:

maria: thanks. we'll schedule the postmortem tomorrow. action owner list: raj (root cause analysis), tess (playbook updates), leo (logs/traces + runbook), samir (monitoring for 2h).

deploy-bot: Canary cp-7265 marked ABORTED (by playbook) — rollout halted and snapshot restored to baseline.

maria: tl;dr — canary with longer context triggered kv-restore regression -> 5xx spike -> feature flag flip + traffic reweight + pod eviction -> service stabilized. Postmortem and follow-ups assigned. Good handoff. :white_check_mark:
